turns.doctor_question: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess I'm here because... things have just been really difficult lately. 

Ever since my father-in-law moved in with us, I've been, I don't know, just snapping at my wife over little house things. I'm also putting off jobs and paperwork that I used to stay on top of without a problem. It's like I just can't seem to get my head quiet anymore. Even when I go out in the workshop to get some space, or if I try to go fishing, my mind just won't shut off.

symptom_reasoning.S060: The patient reports snapping at his wife over minor household matters, which reflects irritability and low frustration tolerance.
symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient describes developing emotional and behavioral difficulties, including irritability, avoidance of responsibilities, and cognitive distress, specifically in response to his father-in-law moving in.

turns.doctor_question: Did these ongoing worries and difficulty quieting your mind begin before your father-in-law moved in?
turns.patient_response: No, it really started after he came to live with us. He moved in after he had a bad fall, and... well, within the first couple of months of him being there, I noticed I was already falling behind on my paperwork. And that's when the arguments with my wife started, mostly over just changes around the house. It definitely wasn't like this before he got here.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms that their functional difficulties and emotional strain developed within a couple of months following an identifiable stressor (father-in-law moving in after a fall).

turns.doctor_question: Since your father-in-law moved in, have you been feeling persistently sad or down?
turns.patient_response: No, I wouldn't really say I feel sad. I mean, I'm not feeling down in the dumps or depressed or anything like that. It's... it's really more just this constant feeling of being wound up. I'm mostly just stressed and frustrated all the time, not really sad.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling sad, down in the dumps, or depressed.
symptom_reasoning.S058: The patient reports a 'constant feeling of being wound up', indicating persistent tension or feeling keyed up.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the situation with your father-in-law, do you find yourself worrying excessively about several other areas of your life?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's pretty much just tied to him being here and how everything at home has changed. I mean, my finances and my health and all that are fine. I don't really worry about those things. It's just the stress from the house that I can't shake.

symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies having excessive worry across multiple domains of life, stating that their worry is strictly tied to the single situation at home.

turns.doctor_question: Since your father-in-law moved in, have you engaged in any behavior that seriously violated rules or other people’s rights?
turns.patient_response: No, definitely not. I haven't done anything like that. I'm just stressed out, I haven't been breaking any rules or getting into trouble or anything.
